title: STMicroelectronics and Hitachi SH-4 CPU Core Architecture, ADCS 7182230F
facts: LDS copies a general-register value into its selected system register. FPUL and FPSCR forms check FPU-disabled state before the update.
A restored PR can name a continuation different from the host C caller. New context-restore code must preserve that guest control transfer.
implementation_scope: Original instructions are byte checked. Existing host fault status -4 is retained for reached FPU-disabled instructions. Only the new restore RTS bypasses the historical ordinary-return contract guard; actual restored targets are dispatched, unknown targets remain missing -2, and status3 propagates the actual668e92 continuation to the live scheduler frame. No guest register, stack, counter or callback result is invented. Other historical code/models/guards are unchanged.
